name: Texas Historical Commission, Archeology Division
availability: Regional archeologists respond to public inquiries about archeological sites and artifacts; use the regional map to reach your area's archeologist.

name: Texas Archeological Stewardship Network (THC)
availability: Volunteer avocational stewards who record sites and private artifact collections and assist THC archeologists.

name: Texas Archeological Society
availability: The contact form routes questions to the business office, a committee or a regional director. Regional chapters below.

name: Houston Archeological Society (TAS chapter)
availability: Monthly meetings on the third Thursday, 6:00–7:45 pm, Trini Mendenhall Community Center, Houston.

name: North Texas Archeological Society (TAS chapter)
availability: Hybrid monthly meetings on the second Thursday, 7:00–8:30 pm (UNT Health Science Center, Fort Worth, or Zoom).

name: Texas Science & Natural History Museum (UT Austin)
availability: In-person fossil identification with a paleontologist by appointment, Tuesday–Saturday 1–4 pm (email to request; regular admission applies). Educational IDs only: no authentications or appraisals.

name: Dallas Paleontological Society
contact: Hotline 817-355-4693 · Fossil Bureau of Investigation: fbi@dallaspaleo.org
availability: The Fossil Bureau of Investigation helps identify fossils and investigate finds, generally within about 100 miles of Dallas.

name: Paleontological Society of Austin
contact: Officer contacts on the society's contact page
availability: Monthly meetings, usually the third Tuesday at 7:00 pm (Austin Gem and Mineral Society, 6719 Burnet Lane). The public is invited; bring finds for identification.

name: Texas Archeological Research Laboratory (UT Austin)
availability: A research collections facility, not a public identification service: TARL does not authenticate or appraise artifacts for private citizens. Research access by appointment.

name: Lubbock Lake Landmark (Museum of Texas Tech University)
availability: General information, research and field opportunities through the Landmark office.

name: Center for Big Bend Studies (Sul Ross State University)
availability: Research center for the archeology and history of the Big Bend region.
